newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares close at new record high but wary.
newsitem.headline: German shares close at new record high but wary.

text.p: German shares, fueled by the dollar, kept up their staggering advance toward record levels in bourse dealings on Monday but traders said they were wary about maintaining the gains for the near-term.

The 30-share DAX index ended bourse trade up 29.31 points at 3,030.68 points, a new record high, while the IBIS DAX, which reflects all-day dealings, was up 14.08 points at 3,020.95 in all-day dealings.
But some market observers said the DAX could soon face a correction as the index reached dizzying heights.
"The party is still going on but the risks are growing," said Trinkaus Capital Management in a commentary. "In the short-term, there are few factors to slow down this market."
But Trinkaus, as well as other traders, noted that the DAX's current levels should prompt some caution and that a correction phase would begin at the latest in February.
Dealings in the afternoon were expected to focus on Wall Street, which kept up its record-setting run on Friday.
Fundamental factors also expected to move the market this week include M3 money supply figures and German producer prices data for December, both expected early this week.
Dealers said they would also be monitoring the Ifo report on German business sentiment, also due early in the week.
Among specific shares, Deutsche Telekom AG was up 41 pfennigs at 31.53 marks, lifted by its announcement that sales grew to more than 63 billion marks.
Telekom, in the unexpected announcement, also said it would pay -- as promised -- a dividend of 60 pfennigs per share on 1996 results and had cut its debt by 10 billion marks.
Interest was also strong in the banking sector, where the higher dollar and low German interest rates prompted interest in the sector, which has been gaining favour with investors.

Deutsche Bank AG gained 2.30 marks to 81.18 marks, reaching a new record high at 81.37 marks despite a squabble with one of its top London fund managers, who has since resigned, and allegations that she sought to lure away top traders when she considered a rival job offer.
Commerzbank AG was up 74 pfennigs at 44.55 marks, while Dresdner was up 1.55 marks at 53.65 marks.
Sportswear group Adidas AG, which has a considerable part of its sales abroad, also benefited from the strong dollar, rising 2.30 marks to 150.80 marks.
